obligations.obligation: CPython 3.13.9; Queue(maxsize=20); four one-job workers; descriptor ownership; conditional 24 outstanding bound and excluded producer/history memory
Successful-put acceptance, per-ID in-session ledger, queued versus running versus terminal progress and thread confinement
Graceful admission closure, non-immediate shutdown, drain/acknowledge accepted work, await workers and retain results
Force-stop abandonment versus active cancellation; no success from qsize/join; no extra acknowledgment of drained jobs
Failure/cancellation never counted as conversion success; exactly one task_done per retrieved item; cancellation before get has none; cooperative stop and external-layer boundary
Component-owned temporary/output paths, validation and publish success gate, cleanup failures, completed-output retention and unspecified destination policy
Retain 12 equal ready jobs, four workers, two seconds: six-second makespan; ideal saturated two jobs/second; no arbitrary-workload or measured-throughput inference
Native shutdown versus conditional older-runtime sentinels; sequential/more workers and CPU execution alternatives
Full draft, all generated criticism and dispositions, preserved supported meaning, legitimate rejections and unresolved questions
Discriminating planned queue/application tests; separate actual execution, upstream test inspection, target version and model measurements

consequential_source_families.family: Conditional capacity and ideal scheduling derivation
consequential_source_families.independent_check: Twelve two-second jobs require 24 worker-seconds, so four workers require at least six seconds; three simultaneous equal waves attain it. Under homogeneous saturation, four completions per two seconds gives two jobs/second.
